title: Why Pipe Sizing Matters: Water Supply Flow & Pressure
description: Sizing water supply lines isn't just about getting water to a tap—it is about controlling flow velocity and friction loss. When supply pipes are undersized, water velocity increases significantly. This causes high friction loss, noisy piping, and dramatic pressure drops whenever a second fixture is turned on. A 3/4-inch (20mm) pipe carries roughly double the flow volume of a 1/2-inch (15mm) pipe due to cross-sectional area differences. Properly sizing trunk lines and branch pipes ensures balanced delivery across all fixtures simultaneously. What pipe sizing issues do you notice most on site?

The internal diameters are cleanly visible at an cutaway end section to visually demonstrate internal flow capacity. Photorealistic, physically accurate plumbing arrangement, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no logos.
visual_story: The viewer instantly notices the physical diameter contrast between a 1/2-inch line and a 3/4-inch line side-by-side inside a wall cavity. The cutaway visual emphasizes cross-sectional area, showing how a slight increase in pipe diameter significantly increases available volume and reduces friction loss.

on_image_text.explanation: Undersized pipes increase water velocity and friction, starving fixtures when used together.
on_image_text.takeaway: Size supply main trunks larger than branch pipes to maintain stable fixture pressure.
